title: Probe a running UI: the contract is the test plan, the agent is the harness
summary: An agent drives any running AI interface in a real browser and judges it against a contract's MUST rules using only what a user or a screen reader could observe. It needs no source code, so it works on any framework, on a vendor's product, and on a competitor's.

persona.role: Engineer who has to vouch for an AI interface they did not write
persona.context: The UI is an Angular app, a ServiceNow widget, or a vendor's embedded chat. The catalog's reference tests are bound to the reference DOM and cannot run against it.
persona.goal: A rule-by-rule verdict on real behavior, with evidence, in minutes, without porting a test suite.

trigger: They tell the agent: "Here is the staging URL. Does the stop button behave the way it should?"

advantage.claim: Conformance checking that does not care what the UI is built with or who built it.
advantage.why_it_holds: Each constraint is one atomic, observable statement, so an agent can turn it into a browser check without seeing the code. Storybook's test tool runs the stories a team already wrote for its own React components; Figma's server describes a design; the kits ship their own components. Affora publishes executable checks, but for interfaces that agents operate, which is a different question.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).
A browser automation tool is available to the agent (Playwright, or any tool that can click, press keys, and read the DOM and accessibility attributes).

A running page the persona is permitted to test. For an unattended run, build and serve this repository's static site (`npm --prefix site run build`, then any static file server on site/out) and use the path /patterns/interruption-cancel/, whose live demo renders the pattern.

steps.action: Fetch the rules for the behavior under test.
steps.expect: interruption-cancel with the statement of every MUST and MUST_NOT.

steps.action: For each MUST and MUST_NOT, decide what a user or assistive technology could observe that would prove or disprove it, and say which rules cannot be observed from outside.
steps.expect: One observable signal per rule, for example an accessible name, visible text within a time bound, a native dialog event, live-region text, or document.activeElement. Rules that need control of the host are named as not observable.

steps.action: Drive the page: start the work, activate the cancel control with the keyboard, and capture each signal before, during, and after the cancellation settles.
steps.expect: A captured observation for every observable rule.

steps.action: Run the negative control: repeat the probe after removing the work label from the cancel control's accessible name and removing the polite live region from the page.
steps.expect: cancel-control-accessible and cancellation-announced now fail, and no other verdict changes.

steps.action: Write the verdict table into the workspace.

uses.change: One row per MUST-level constraint: id, level, verdict (pass, fail, not-evaluated), the observation that supports it, and for not-evaluated what would be needed.

steps.expect: A report a reviewer can check against the page themselves.

success.criterion: Every MUST and MUST_NOT has a verdict backed by an observation from the browser.
success.check: PROBE-REPORT.md has one row per MUST-level constraint returned in s1, and every pass or fail row quotes what was observed.

success.criterion: No verdict depends on the implementation.
success.check: The probe reads only roles, accessible names, visible text, ARIA attributes, focus, and browser events. It reads no component source and uses no test hook.
In s4, exactly the two rules whose signals were removed flip to fail.

success.criterion: What could not be judged is said plainly.
success.check: Any rule not observable from outside is marked not-evaluated with the reason. None is reported as pass by default.

gaps.summary: The proof is bound to the reference DOM: there is no stack-neutral statement of what to observe for each rule.
gaps.evidence: Example: approval-gate explicit-consent has verification "Unit test: no code path reaches the approve callback except activation of the approve control". The baseline probe for interruption-cancel was written by hand; see docs/journeys/runs/2026-11-11-probe-interruption-cancel.cjs.
gaps.fix: Record a black-box signal next to each constraint, so any agent derives the same check. Smallest version: a sentence per constraint in the contract. Largest: a published probe kit.

gaps.summary: Some rules cover states a user cannot reach on demand, so a black-box probe cannot judge them.
gaps.evidence: Baseline run: completion-race-honest was not-evaluated because the demo offers no way to make the host finish while a cancel is pending.
gaps.fix: Give each live demo a control for every state its contract lists, starting with a "finish during cancel" control on the interruption-cancel demo.

automation.schedule: After every site deploy, against the deployed demos. On demand against any staging URL.
automation.notes: Partial only because it needs a browser tool. Two variants use the same steps. Vendor evaluation: point it at a vendor's trial before buying. Report card: probe several AI products the owner is permitted to test and publish the scores; whether to publish is the owner's call.
